title: Native Windows Gateway: browser control blocked by listener-owner verification
subtitle: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node #1975
author: heekwonlee74-cmd
body:
Windows Companion 2026.9.8-1; Gateway MSIX 2026.10.900.0; CLI 2026.10.9. Native isolated-session-v1 setup, without SSH or a managed WSL Gateway.

Agent chat works and browser.proxy is approved. However, requesting tabs with the user browser profile fails: “Browser control authentication was blocked because the local listener owner could not be verified.”

Restarting the Gateway restored basic connectivity. Changing the security preset from Locked Down to Recommended did not resolve the browser error.

Source review suggests that the non-SSH browser authorization callback requires ResolveManagedDistroName, while that method returns null for native-package Gateways. Could this reject a valid native Gateway? This is our analysis, not a maintainer-confirmed diagnosis.

Please confirm a supported fix or compatible version combination that preserves existing conversations and settings without disabling ownership verification. Related reports: #1333 and #1691.

comments.author: heekwonlee74-cmd
comments.body: Update: Chat and a weather search returned a response in the Windows desktop app, but when I asked OpenClaw to add six packs of Hetbahn to a Coupang cart, it reported that browser control was still blocked by the listener-owner verification error. OpenClaw reported that it could not check the Coupang login status and that no cart changes or payment were made.

comments.author: heekwonlee74-cmd
comments.body:
Update: This still reproduces with Windows Companion 2026.11.1 and OpenClaw CLI 2026.11.1.

I corrected the browser node target from a disconnected node to the currently connected, approved Windows node, then restarted the Windows app. The node reconnected successfully, but both `openclaw browser status --json` and `openclaw browser doctor --json` still fail with:

`Browser control authentication was blocked because the local listener owner could not be verified.`

No authentication checks were disabled and no permissions were expanded. Is there an official fix or supported recovery procedure for this native Windows Gateway setup that preserves existing conversations, settings, and listener-owner verification?

comments.author: roboclaw-bot
comments.body:
Consolidating this report into #1701 (Native Gateway: browser status/profiles blocked by listener ownership verification). Both reports hit the same production gap: a non-SSH Native Gateway has no managed WSL distro, and the browser-listener callback falls back to a fixture-only check before sending HTTP credentials. This is not fixed. Your November 9 confirmation on Companion/CLI 2026.11.1 remains important evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1975#issuecomment-6730900436. Keeping #1701 open for native browser-port attestation and status/profiles proof, including rejection of foreign/replaced listeners. No ownership checks should be disabled.
